extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, inventors, legal researchers, and drafters of patent applications referencing Title 35
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes transitional, effective-date, severability, and repeal-related provisions of Title 35 (Patents) as enacted July 19, 1952, and notes select amendments and mapping of former sections to new sections. Intended to guide how the statutory rules apply across time and to existing/pending patents and applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and general applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This Act shall take effect on January 1, 1953 and shall apply to all applications for patent filed on or after such date and to all patents granted on such applications. It shall apply to further proceedings on applications pending on such date and to patents granted on such applications except as otherwise provided. It shall apply to unexpired patents granted prior to such date except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the baseline temporal scope of Title 35: primary rule is prospective application to filings and patents as of Jan. 1, 1953, but several specific exceptions and savings provisions follow in subsections (b)–(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retroactivity of section 102(d) to existing patents and pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 102(d) of Title 35, as enacted by section 1 hereof, shall not apply to existing patents and pending applications, but the law previously in effect, namely the first paragraph of R. S. 4887 [first paragraph of section 32 of former Title 35], shall apply to such patents and applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves the pre-enactment novelty/related provisions for patents/applications that existed at the enactment date; practitioners should determine which statutory regime (pre-1953 law vs. enacted Title 35) governs a given application/patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retroactivity of Section 119 (second paragraph) to existing patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 119, second paragraph, of Title 35 as enacted by section 1 hereof shall not apply to existing patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that certain priority/foreign-filing-related provisions in section 119 do not affect patents already in existence at enactment; evaluate priority claims accordingly for pre-enactment patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace-period rule for pre-August 5, 1940 filings (section 102(b) adjustment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of one year specified in section 102(b) of Title 35 as enacted by section 1 hereof shall not apply in the case of applications filed before August 5, 1940, and patents granted on such applications, and with respect to such applications and patents, said period is two years instead of one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For older filings (before Aug. 5, 1940) the pre-existing two-year bar/grace period continues to apply rather than the new one-year period; practitioners handling very old filings/patents must account for the longer pre-1953 timing rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of prior judicial findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing contained in Title 35, as enacted by section 1 hereof, shall operate to nullify any judicial finding prior to the effective date of this Act on the validity of any patent by a court of competent jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court decisions rendered before Jan. 1, 1953 that affect patent validity remain operative and are not implicitly overturned by enactment of Title 35; check pre-existing case law when assessing consequences for specific patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-impairment of Atomic Energy Act provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in Title 35, as enacted by section 1 hereof, shall affect any provision of the Atomic Energy Act of 1946 (Aug. 1, 1946, ch. 724, 60 Stat. 755) [§ 2011 et seq. of Title 42, The Public Health and Welfare].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that Title 35 does not displace or alter the operation of provisions in the Atomic Energy Act; special statutory regimes (e.g., secrecy, patenting of atomic energy inventions) remain governed by that Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-application of certain Title 35 timing provision (section 4) to earlier-filed applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of one year specified in section 4 of Title 35 as enacted by section 1 hereof shall not apply in the case of applications filed before the effective date of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Another explicit transitional rule preserving earlier timing rules for pre-effective-date filings; confirm which section 4 timing rule is implicated when analyzing pre-1953 applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeals do not affect existing rights or liabilities; secrecy orders continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 5 ... repealed the sections or parts of sections of the Revised Statutes or Statutes at Large codified in this Act with the proviso that 'Any rights or liabilities now existing under such sections or parts thereof shall not be affected by this repeal.' An order of secrecy issued under or in effect under the repealed Act and in effect on the date of approval of this Act, shall be considered as issued under this Act, and any claims arising under the repealed Act or subject to presentation and determination pursuant thereto and unsettled as of the effective date of this Act, may be presented and determined pursuant to the provisions of this Act [this title].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves substantive rights/liabilities from the repealed statutes and carries over secrecy orders into the new statutory regime; transitional procedures exist for claims under the prior law to be handled under Title 35.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separability / severability clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3 ... provided that: 'If any provision of Title 35, as enacted by section 1 hereof, is declared unconstitutional or is held invalid, the validity of the remainder of this title shall not be affected.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard severability rule: invalidation of part of the statute does not automatically void the remainder; when assessing the impact of judicial invalidation, treat other provisions as presumptively intact unless otherwise held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table showing disposition of former sections (section mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: A table mapping former sections of Title 35 to the new sections (e.g., former section 1 → new section 1; former 11 → new 31, 32; former 34 → new 113, 114; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides cross-reference mapping to assist in locating how pre-enactment statutory provisions correspond to current Title 35 sections; useful for historical research and applying prior authorities to current section numbers.
